card.name: Inside opening clauses before a contrast
card.fires_on: Words just after the subject or verb of an introductory clause such as "Although X", "While X", "Besides" or "In this lesson,". The next part of the sentence is expected to turn to a main point or contrast.

modes.label: Concessive clause verb
modes.description: The verb right after the subject in a clause starting with Although or While.
modes.example: While Melville<< will>> always be legendary for his epic novel,

modes.label: Lesson summary opener
modes.description: The subject word "students" after an introductory phrase in lesson descriptions.
modes.example: In this American exploration lesson,<< students>> research the events that led to Columbus finding

modes.label: Besides or in addition
modes.description: The word that continues a phrase like "Besides" or "In addition" before an extra point.
modes.example: In addition<< to>> aesthetically improving your lawn area,

card.writes: It leans toward odd or foreign-script tokens and away from contrast words like "but" and "versus", so there is no clear output effect on the sentence.
card.plain: It lights up in the middle of an opening phrase like "Although X is..." or "In this lesson, students...", before the main point arrives.
